_meta.source: CDC Travelers' Health (wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel) + WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality (2022)
_meta.note: Country-level tap water safety. Coarse-grained by necessity — most countries don't publish per-region data the way the UK DWI does. For the UK, the app falls through to the detailed Severn Trent / Thames / etc. lookup instead.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.notes: High-quality regulated tap water. See your supplier for detailed report.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.notes: Safe to drink. Some rural areas use group water schemes — check locally.

countries.name: United States
countries.notes: EPA-regulated, generally safe. Lead concerns in some older buildings.

countries.name: Canada
countries.notes: Generally safe across most of the country.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended for drinking. Use bottled water. Mexico City and resort areas often have filtered systems, but variability is high.

recommendations.primary: Buy sealed bottled water from any convenience store (OXXO is everywhere) or supermarket. Bigger 1.5L or 5L bottles work out cheaper and use less plastic than small ones. Use it for drinking AND brushing your teeth.
avoid: Raw salads / unpeeled fruit washed in tap water
Drinks topped up with tap water
travel_filter: LifeStraw Go bottle (£35) — fill from any tap, drink instantly

countries.name: France
countries.notes: Safe to drink across most of the country, including Paris.

countries.name: Germany
countries.notes: Strictly regulated; one of the most-tested water supplies in Europe.

countries.name: Spain
countries.notes: Safe in cities. Taste varies; bottled water common at restaurants.

countries.name: Italy
countries.notes: Safe nationwide. 'Acqua non potabile' signs mark exceptions.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.notes: Safe to drink.

countries.name: Greece
countries.notes: Safe in Athens and major cities; many islands rely on shipped or desalinated water with variable taste.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.notes: Among the cleanest in the world. Public fountains often drinkable.

countries.name: Austria
countries.notes: Alpine spring water; drink freely.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.notes: Excellent quality, no chlorine taste.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.notes: Safe to drink.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.notes: Very high quality.

countries.name: Norway
countries.notes: Glacier-fed in many regions. Drink freely.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.notes: Drawn from protected groundwater. Safe.

countries.name: Finland
countries.notes: Excellent. Among the world's cleanest.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.notes: Filtered through volcanic rock. Among the purest globally.

countries.name: Australia
countries.notes: Safe nationwide.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.notes: Generally safe. A few rural areas have advisories — check locally.

countries.name: Japan
countries.notes: Strictly regulated and tested. Safe nationwide.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.notes: Treated to high standards. Many locals prefer bottled out of taste preference.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.notes: PUB-managed, fully potable.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended. Bottled or boiled water for drinking.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water from any 7-Eleven (they're everywhere). Most hotels leave free bottled water in your room — top up from there.
avoid: Bag ice from carts (cubes in restaurants are usually fine)
Drinks topped up with tap water

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended. Bottled or boiled.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water from any convenience store. Hotels usually leave free bottles in your room. Sealed cans of soft drinks and beer are safe.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.notes: Tap water not safe to drink. Use bottled or boil for 1 min+.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water from any Indomaret or Alfamart store. Bali especially needs care — tap is not safe even in good hotels.
avoid: Salads / fresh juices unless from clean tourist spots

countries.name: India
countries.notes: Tap water not safe. Use sealed bottled or filtered water.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water only. Always check the cap is intact — refilled bottles are a common scam. Big brands are most reliable.
avoid: Fresh juice / lassi from street stalls
travel_filter: GRAYL Ultrapress (£90) — basically essential for India

countries.name: Egypt
countries.notes: Tap water not safe. Bottled water only.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water from supermarkets — Carrefour, Spinneys, or hotel shops. Check the cap is intact.

countries.name: Peru
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended. Bottled only.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water. Coca tea (mate de coca, boiled) is safe everywhere and helps with altitude in Cusco / Sacred Valley.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.notes: Cities have treated water; visitors usually drink bottled.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water from any épicerie (corner shop). Mint tea is everywhere and boiled — safe.
avoid: Tap water for brushing teeth (in older buildings)

countries.name: Turkey
countries.notes: Chlorinated and treated but locals nearly all drink bottled.

recommendations.primary: Sealed bottled water from any market or convenience store. Locals drink bottled too — tap water tastes heavily chlorinated.
avoid: Tap water for drinking and brushing

countries.name: Philippines
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended outside of major hotels.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.notes: Generally needs boiling. Some KL districts have safe tap water.

countries.name: India
countries.notes: Tap water not safe. Use sealed bottled or filtered water.

countries.name: China
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended for drinking. Boiled water served at most restaurants.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.notes: Treated to drinkable standards; locals often filter or boil out of caution.

countries.name: Hong Kong
countries.notes: Treated and safe, though older plumbing can affect taste.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.notes: Desalinated and treated. Safe at source but old building tanks can affect quality.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.notes: Treated but most residents drink bottled.

countries.name: Israel
countries.notes: Safe to drink nationwide.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.notes: Tap water not safe. Bottled water only.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.notes: Cities have treated water; visitors usually drink bottled.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.notes: Safe in major cities; rural areas variable.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.notes: Treated but most residents use filters or bottled. Generally not recommended raw for visitors.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.notes: Safe in Buenos Aires and major cities. Rural variability.

countries.name: Chile
countries.notes: Safe in Santiago and most cities. High mineral content in north.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.notes: Treated in Bogotá and Medellín. Bottled elsewhere.

countries.name: Peru
countries.notes: Tap water not recommended. Bottled only.

countries.name: Turkey
countries.notes: Chlorinated and treated but locals nearly all drink bottled.

countries.name: Russia
countries.notes: Quality varies. Bottled or filtered recommended.

countries.name: Poland
countries.notes: Safe in major cities; some older buildings have pipe-quality issues.

countries.name: Czech Republic
countries.notes: Safe to drink.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.notes: Safe; Budapest known for its mineral-rich water.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.notes: Safe to drink nationwide.
